items.title: [@connorbritain/mssql-mcp-core] mssql-mcp-core: SQL injection in mssql-mcp write tools via unparameterized table names and WHERE clauses
items.summary: Several tools in mssql-mcp-core built T-SQL by string-interpolating caller-supplied identifiers and predicates directly into the statement passed to the node-mssql Request.query() batch API. Only data values were parameterized.Affected tools and inputs:update_data, delete_data: tableName and the free-form whereClause were interpolated raw.insert_data: tableName and column names (object keys) were interpolated raw.execute_transaction: the same raw tableName/whereClause interpolation per operation.create_table, create_index, drop_table: table/column/index/schema identifiers were interpolated with no or insufficient validation.list_databases (reader tier): the stateFilter argument was interpolated raw into the query, with only a non-enforced inputSchema enum guarding it.The only check on whereClause was that it was non-empty. Because the row-count and preview queries run before the confirmUpdate/confirmDelete step, a malicious whereClause or tableName executed on the first call, bypassing the preview/confirmation and maxRows safety controls. Request.query() submits a multi-statement T-SQL batch, so a crafted input enabled stacked statements (arbitrary DDL/DML), sub-selects, and (with a privileged login and xp_cmdshell enabled) OS command execution. Because list_databases is a read-only tool, the stateFilter sink makes the reader package injectable as well.ImpactAn actor who can supply tool arguments (a malicious or compromised MCP client, or an LLM agent steered via indirect prompt injection) could read, modify, or drop arbitrary data, bypass the read_data allow/deny validation and the preview/confirmation/maxRows safeguards, and conditionally achieve OS command execution.PatchesFixed in @connorbritain/mssql-mcp-core 0.6.0:All identifiers are validated against a strict allowlist and bracket-quoted via a shared helper.The free-form whereClause string parameter is removed (breaking change) and replaced with structured, parameterized filters ({ column, operator, value }) using an operator allowlist. Values are always bound, never interpolated.list_databases validates stateFilter against a fixed allowlist before use.Upgrade the consumer packages: mssql-mcp-reader 0.5.0, mssql-mcp-writer 0.5.0, mssql-mcp-server 0.6.0 (all depend on core ^0.6.0).WorkaroundsUpgrading is the only complete fix; the list_databases (stateFilter) sink is reachable even under READONLY=true and in the reader package. As defense in depth, run the server under a least-privilege SQL login with xp_cmdshell disabled, and restrict which MCP clients can invoke the tools.Referenceshttps://github.com/ConnorBritain/mssql-mcp-core/security/advisories/GHSA-2m9m-6cr5-9x25https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63129https://github.com/ConnorBritain/mssql-mcp-core/pull/1https://github.com/ConnorBritain/mssql-mcp-core/commit/227e2efc4e3311c477b7ae509c3ae15437a4f815https://github.com/ConnorBritain/mssql-mcp-core/commit/a9727f83768598e4fdbddfbc717ccfebb84ae7afhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2m9m-6cr5-9x25

items.title: [install-artifact-from-github] install-artifact-from-github loads downloaded native artifacts without integrity verification
items.summary: Descriptionbin/install-from-cache.js downloads a prebuilt native addon (*.node) over the network and writes it directly to the artifact path with no cryptographic integrity verification of any kind — no checksum manifest, no signature, no SRI. A scan of the whole package for createHash|sha256|checksum|integrity|digest|signature finds nothing. The file is then require()-loaded by the consumer, which executes the addon's native module-init code. Anyone able to influence the download achieves code execution on the installing machine.Affected code (v1.6.0)Mirror is fully attacker-steerable via an env var, no host pinning — bin/install-from-cache.js:80:let assetUrl = mirrorHost || process.env[mirrorEnvVar] || 'https://github.com';re2 passes --host-var RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR, so setting RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR (CI config, .npmrc/env passthrough, a compromised CI job, a poisoned shell profile) redirects 100% of the download to an arbitrary host with zero pinning.The write sink is a bare writeFile, no verification — bin/install-from-cache.js:185-187:const write = async (name, data) => {  await fsp.mkdir(path.dirname(name), {recursive: true});  await fsp.writeFile(name, data);   // `data` is the raw HTTP response body};Cleartext transfer + silent protocol downgrade on redirect — bin/install-from-cache.js:155,165:const httpLib = isHttps.test(url) ? https : isHttp.test(url) ? http : null;   // http:// supported...get(res.headers.location).then(resolve, reject);   // re-derives protocol from the NEW urlAn https:// asset that 302-redirects to http:// is followed and fetched over plaintext, no warning, no scheme pinning, no redirect cap.The post-download "verification" is not an integrity gateisVerified() optionally runs npm run verify-build / npm test after writing the file. For re2, scripts/verify-build.js require()s the binary as its first line — i.e. the downloaded addon's native code has already executed by the time any check runs. It is a functional smoke test, not an integrity gate, and it is skipped entirely when any npm_config_platform* env var is set (:120-122).Proof of conceptA self-contained, non-malicious PoC (poc.js) proves the missing-integrity property against the real install-from-cache, without shipping a weaponized binary: it stands up a plaintext-HTTP "mirror" serving a sentinel payload, runs install-from-cache with RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR pointed at it, and shows the served bytes are written verbatim to build/Release/re2.node:npm i install-artifact-from-githubIAFG_BIN=./node_modules/install-artifact-from-github/bin/install-from-cache.js node poc.jsattacker mirror (plaintext http) on 127.0.0.1:PORT  [mirror] served 2083 attacker bytes over HTTP for /uhop/node-re2/releases/download/1.24.1/darwin-arm64-137Writing to build/Release/re2.node ... Done.install-from-cache exit: 0served   sha256: ec6fdde6...4ebcwritten  sha256: ec6fdde6...4ebc✓ attacker bytes written VERBATIM to build/Release/re2.node — NO integrity check rejected themThe install succeeds (exit 0) with attacker-controlled bytes at the artifact path. Because a real .node executes on require() (NAPI/NODE_MODULE init), substituting a malicious one yields code execution in the installing/running process. (A full code-execution harness using a benign marker-writing native addon was verified separately and is available on request; withheld here to avoid shipping executable payloads.)Attack scenarios (any one suffices)Attacker-configured or later-compromised RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR.Tampered GitHub release / compromised maintainer account — no checksum detects a swapped asset, even over HTTPS.On-path attacker where a plaintext (http://) mirror or an https→http redirect is in play.Suggested fixPublish per-release SHASUMS256.txt (or embed expected digests) and verify the download's SHA-256 before writing/loading; refuse on mismatch. (This is the model prebuild-install already uses.)Reject http:// asset URLs and https→http redirect downgrades; pin scheme across redirects; cap redirect count/hosts.Document that verify-build/test run after load and cannot gate integrity.PoCpoc.js:// PoC — install-artifact-from-github writes a network-downloaded artifact to disk with NO// integrity verification, from an env-controlled mirror, over plaintext HTTP.//// This proves the CORE defect (arbitrary attacker-supplied bytes become build/Release/re2.node// with zero checksum/signature check) WITHOUT shipping a weaponized native binary: we serve a// sentinel payload and show byte-for-byte (sha256) that it is written verbatim as the artifact.// Because a .node artifact is dlopen()'d on require (running its module-init native code), an// attacker who substitutes it — via a compromised/attacker-set RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR, a tampered// GitHub release, or an on-path MITM on the plaintext path — achieves code execution.//// Run:  IAFG_BIN=/path/to/install-artifact-from-github/bin/install-from-cache.js node poc.js//       (defaults to require.resolve if install-artifact-from-github is installed
